messages:
maria: Heads-up — our March 10 invoice has a weird $12,300 line: "DataTransfer-InterRegion" + an extra "EC2:g4dn.xlarge" bill that doesn't match our fleet. Did anyone else notice this?

billing-bot: New invoice uploaded: https://invoices.redwood.example/INV-2026-03-10 (internal link) :page_facing_up:

oliver: I see the invoice, looking at cost-explorer now. Can you paste the raw line item (account, product, usage type)?

maria: Paste from the PDF: "Account: prod-us-west; Product: AmazonEC2; UsageType: USW2-G4DN-Box; Amount: $9,800" then "Product: AWS-DataTransfer; UsageType: InterRegion-GB; Amount: $2,500"

kevin: Ran a quick CE query, grouping by tag and usage type. Looks like the g4dn hours for 3/9-3/10 are double counted in two linked billing accounts. snippet: ```aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-03-09,End=2026-03-11 --granularity=DAILY --metrics UnblendedCost --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=USAGE_TYPE``` output: 
2026-03-09 g4dn.xlarge $4,900
2026-03-10 g4dn.xlarge $9,800 (duplicated)

raj: Could be a consolidation issue when we moved prod-us-west under the new org root at month boundary. If tags/linked-account ids changed, Cost Explorer can show duplicates because both payer and linked account are billed. Check master/payer settings.

oliver: Agreed. Can someone check whether we had overlapping Reserved Instance/Savings Plan tags? That sometimes makes usage appear twice (RI amortization + on-demand line).

kevin: Checked RI utilization report — RIs show correct, but there's an extra amortized charge coming from the old billing account. Looks like the old account didn't transfer RI ownership before consolidation so both accounts got amortized credits and on-demand charges.

maria: Ugh. That explains the double EC2 amount. What about the InterRegion DT $2.5k?

kevin: Inter-region traffic: we had a batch of checkpoint syncs on 3/9 for model shard migration between us-west-2 and us-east-1. The transfer should have been under internal-tagged traffic and netted by peering, but the peer config change on 3/08 caused traffic to route via public IPs for ~6 hours — billed as inter-region data transfer. Evidence: VPC flow logs + transfer bytes matching invoice.

raj: Next steps: 1) open provider billing case for duplicate EC2 RI amortization, 2) request data-transfer credit for the 6-hr window due to config regression, 3) reconcile accounting entries and hold payment until credits/adjustments confirmed. I'll open the support case.

maria: Please include ticket IDs and estimated timeline in the thread. Finance needs to know if we should withhold payment for that invoice.

raj: Support case opened: AWS#987654321 — flagged as potential duplicate amortization. Also opened networking support for data-transfer routing: AWS#987654322. Attached provider case links in billing system. ETA initial response 24–48h.

billing-bot: Billing case created: https://support.aws.amazon.com/cases/987654321

oliver: For internal ops: create a checklist so we don't leave RI ownership during org moves. Also add a canary to VPC peering changes that checks egress path to avoid cross-region public routing.

kevin: Filed infra action items: INFRA-4321 (RI transfer checklist), INFRA-4322 (VPC-peering canary).

maria: Thanks. Finance: I'm marking invoice INV-2026-03-10 as disputed in our ledger and will pause payment for the disputed portion until credits applied. Will update once AWS confirms. :white_check_mark:

raj: Update 2026-03-12 14:12 UTC — AWS confirmed duplicate amortization, issuing credit of $9,800. Data-transfer credit under review. They'll post both as adjustments to next billing.

maria: Excellent. Please keep the thread updated when credits post. If the data-transfer isn't credited, we need to escalate.

kevin: Noted. I'll add automated alerts so next org move triggers a billing pre-check.

oliver: Thanks team. Short-term: finance dispute filed, infra tickets created, support cases open.

maria: Closing loop for now — will re-open if credits don't show by next invoice. :lock:
